Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries yielded 321 hits and 228 unique package paths. The png, png decoder, and image png result windows each stopped at 100; png reader yielded 12 and png parser yielded 9. The HTML search pages do not provide an overall total, so none is inferred. Five named documentation leads remain unresolved and eligible parsers may lie outside these windows. Several packages wrap or fork Go image/png and two use libvips, so 20 package paths do not imply 20 independent engines. One pinned TinyGo PNG decoder panicked on the valid control and is excluded. The one 2×1 pixel control only proves the observed parsing path. Package-level importer counts are adoption signals, not downloads, and absent values are not inferred.

Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries saved 333 hits and 271 unique package paths. The zip, archive zip, and unzip result pages were truncated at 100 each; zip reader returned 23 and zip parser returned 10. The HTML pages did not expose a total result count, so none is inferred. 8 named plausible leads remain unresolved. Search hits are discovery material, not parser evidence, and eligible packages may exist outside these windows. Many verified packages wrap or fork Go archive/zip, so 23 package paths do not imply 23 independent engines. One pinned itchio/arkive ZIP reader passed the control but lacked open-source license evidence and was excluded. The shared one-entry DEFLATE control does not cover other ZIP features. Importer counts are package-level adoption signals from pkg.go.dev at one snapshot date; missing values are not invented.

Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries saved 133 hits and 124 unique package paths. Query windows returned 100, 10, 11, 12, 0 hits in order; the broad mp4 window stopped at 100. The HTML pages give no total result count, so none is inferred. Ten plausible leads remain unresolved, including readers for fragmented MP4 that require a different valid control. Search hits are leads, not evidence. Several verified packages share mp4ff, joy4, gomedia, jfbus, or dhowden/tag code lineages, so the package count does not imply independent parser engines. A single progressive isom MP4 with two tracks and a title proves only the labeled API paths. Importer counts are pkg.go.dev package-level adoption signals, not downloads; zero means no visible direct importers in this snapshot.

Five npm queries saved 495 hits (the id3v2 query returned only 95), covering 447 unique names. Four query result sets were truncated at 100; hits are not all investigated and qualified packages may exist beyond these windows. 10 named plausible leads remain unresolved. Verified packages include tag-only parsers, duration readers, MP3 decoders, and wrappers over shared music-metadata, node-id3, or mpg123 implementations. Duration APIs report different values because of encoder delay/padding, so the expected result is package-specific and recorded. The single control covers ID3v2.3 with three text fields and a one-second tone, not all ID3 or MP3 variants. Browser APIs do not expose tags.

PyPI has no public relevance-ranked keyword search API in this workflow, so the Simple JSON project index was filtered by seven name substrings. The filters matched 210, 21, 19, 71, 143, 14, and 54 project names respectively; the first 100 case-insensitive alphabetical matches were saved per filter, 379 distinct names in total. Alphabetical windows can miss relevant and highly adopted packages, so project documentation supplied additional leads. Eight plausible leads remain unresolved, including a PNG decoder without a macOS wheel, a headless loader that could not import, and packages requiring separate environments. Several accepted packages delegate to Pillow, ImageIO, libvips, or other native engines; 21 package paths do not mean 21 independent decoder engines. The two valid controls prove only the labeled pixel, header, chunk, or tEXt scopes. Tkinter PhotoImage is verified separately on bundled Tk 8.6 and may be absent in other Python distributions. PyPI Stats downloads are a within-Python adoption proxy; byteparse returned HTTP 404 for this metric and remains unranked.

The PyPI Simple JSON project index was filtered by nine package-name substrings, retaining up to 100 case-insensitive alphabetical hits per term. The 418 saved hits contain 407 distinct names but are not a popularity search; relevant packages outside the windows may be missed. Six plausible leads remain unresolved, including the high-download zipfile-deflate64 whose source build failed on this macOS ARM/Python 3.13 host. The 20 verified distribution paths include many wrappers/backports over CPython zipfile; they are not 20 independent ZIP engines. The Zstandard reader was tested on a valid method-93 ZIP made by a pinned generator; other packages used the one-entry DEFLATE control. One entry is a local archive extractor backed by an external unzip utility, recorded as such. The four separate standard-library APIs share underlying ZIP code. Each control proves only its stated compression method, member, and API scope.

The PyPI Simple JSON project index was filtered by nine project-name substrings, retaining at most 100 case-insensitive alphabetical hits per term. The 672 saved hits contain 667 distinct names, but these alphabetic windows are not popularity-ranked and may miss relevant projects. Eight plausible leads remain unresolved, including decord without a compatible host wheel and mediapy failing against the local FFmpeg version. The 20 verified paths include several wrappers over FFmpeg, OpenCV, TagLib, MediaInfo, and other shared engines; family labels distinguish package paths from independent MP4 implementations. The valid one-frame 2x2 H.264/AAC control proves only the recorded box, metadata, audio, or video scope. No CPython 3.13 standard-library MP4 reader is documented in the scoped official index.

The PyPI Simple JSON project-name index was filtered by 16 name substrings, retaining at most 100 case-insensitive alphabetical matches per term. The PyPI Simple JSON index was filtered by ten project-name substrings, retaining at most 100 case-insensitive alphabetical matches per term. The 793 saved hits contain 789 distinct project names; these windows are not popularity-ranked and may miss relevant packages. Six plausible leads remain unresolved, including one valid-control CRLF failure, one undocumented local API, and one C extension build failure. The 22 verified package paths include h11 forks and picohttpparser wrappers, recorded by family rather than claimed as independent implementations. parse-http-header-line and parserheader prove header-field parsing only; websockets proves an HTTP/1.1 handshake request head only. Twenty-one distinct Python distribution paths returned the correct vertices and face count from one valid ASCII PLY 1.0 triangle. This exceeds the 20 working goal but remains below the original 30 ceiling. The paths are not independent decoder engines: PyVista and vedo use VTK, pyminiply and pyvista-miniply use miniply, and assimp-py and pyassimp use Assimp; families are labeled. The single control proves the three-vertex, one-face ASCII subset only, not colors, arbitrary properties, other polygon sizes, or binary PLY. Twelve bounded, alphabetically ordered PyPI name windows saved 668 hits and 666 distinct names; broad substring windows are noisy and can omit packages beyond the first 100. Project documentation supplied additional candidates. Seven plausible leads remain unresolved, including packages requiring native dependencies or specialized PLY controls. pyassimp used system Assimp 6.0.6, and openmesh required CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 for its source build; fresh environments may need these stated conditions. All verified packages received one PyPI Stats last-month metric, but download counts reflect distribution adoption and not independent parser use. Discovery is partial and other qualified packages may remain outside the saved windows.

The PyPI Simple JSON project index was filtered by 12 name substrings. The first 100 case-insensitive alphabetical matches per filter were saved, yielding 675 hits and 669 unique names; name windows have no popularity ordering and can miss relevant packages. Project docs supplied additional candidates. Six plausible leads remain unresolved, including source-only/native bindings and generic image readers. The 20 verified distribution paths include 18 P3 pixel readers, one P2 pixel reader, and one P3 dimensions-only reader; several share Pillow, Qt, or netpbmfile parser families. These paths are not 20 independent decoder engines and control success proves only the labeled variant and output scope. The local bundled Tk 8.6 PhotoImage API rejected valid P1/P2/P3 controls despite broad official PPM/PGM documentation, so no standard API is counted for this ASCII cell. PyPI Stats initially rate-limited one request; a later successful retry supplied its within-Python download metric.

Twenty distinct package paths have passed valid Matrix Market controls, meeting the working goal of 20; the original ceiling remains 30. Thirteen case-insensitive PyPI Simple index name filters retained the first 100 alphabetical matches per term, saving 379 hits and 378 distinct names. These windows are not popularity-ranked and miss documented projects without matching names; targeted documentation searches found AmbiDose, PIASO, and scinterop outside the name windows. Three explored leads remain unresolved: pysparse and sppy builds, and vectorphile lacking a documented input API. fast_mtx_reader was excluded after a valid control produced an incorrect matrix. Verified rows include wrappers over SciPy/fast_matrix_market, labeled by family rather than claimed as independent parser cores. The controls cover coordinate real general and symmetric matrices, basic graph topology, and one 10x integer count matrix; array, pattern, and complex variants remain untested. Six last-month download metrics remain unranked: subgraphsearch and sdos returned HTTP 404; mtl5, scab, DOTools-py, and piaso-tools returned HTTP 429. No values were inferred. scprep uses Python 3.10 because its pinned pandas dependency lacks a Python 3.13 wheel; mtl5 uses a Python 3.10 macOS wheel because its Python 3.13 source build failed on a missing hwy/highway.h header; scprep's pinned source LICENSE is MIT despite conflicting PyPI metadata. The working target is met, but discovery remains partial and three plausible leads are unresolved.
